'''Gerald Lee Alexanderson''' (November 13, 1933 – December 16, 2020) was an American mathematician who studied [[combinatorics]] and [[number theory]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Obituary for Gerald ("Jerry") L. Alexanderson |url=https://newsroom.maa.org/121385-obituary-for-gerald-jerry-l-alexanderson |date=December 22, 2020 |website=Mathematical Association of America |access-date=February 20, 2021 |archive-date=September 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230929133416/https://newsroom.maa.org/121385-obituary-for-gerald-jerry-l-alexanderson |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was the Michael & Elizabeth Valeriote Professor of Science at [[Santa Clara University]], and in 1997–1998 was president of the [[Mathematical Association of America]]. He was also president of [[The Fibonacci Association]] from 1980 to 1984.<ref name="maa">[http://www.maa.org/about-maa/governance/maa-presidents/gerald-lee-alexanderson-1997-1998-maa-president Gerald Lee Alexanderson, 1997-1998 MAA President], MAA Presidents, [[Mathematical Association of America]], retrieved 2014-06-26.</ref><ref name="cv"/>

==Education and career==
Alexanderson did his undergraduate studies at the [[University of Oregon]], graduating with a B.A. in 1955. He earned a master's degree from [[Stanford University]] in 1958, and in the same year joined the [[Santa Clara University]] faculty. At Santa Clara, he chaired the Department of Mathematics (later the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science) for 35 years, from 1967 to 2002.<ref name="maa"/><ref name="cv">[http://math.scu.edu/~galexand/glacvweb.html Curriculum vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220116180456/https://math.scu.edu/~galexand/glacvweb.html |date=2022-01-16 }}, retrieved 2014-06-26.</ref> He also served as the Division Director of Physical Sciences and Mathematics.<ref name=":0" /> Abraham Hillman was his most frequent co-author.<ref>{{cite news|title=Memorial: Abraham Hillman *50|year=2004|newspaper=Princeton Alumni Weekly|url=https://paw.princeton.edu/memorial/abraham-hillman-50}}</ref> As a student, his greatest influences have been [[Ivan M. Niven|Ivan Niven]] and [[George Pólya]].<ref name=":0" />

He was the co-author, editor, or co-editor of 15 books. He served as the editor of ''[[Mathematics Magazine]]'' from 1986 to 1990,<ref name="maa"/><ref name="cv"/> and was the associate editor of ''[[The American Mathematical Monthly]]'' and ''[[The College Mathematics Journal]]''.<ref name=":0" />

He actively promoted competitions in mathematics, and served as the associate director of the [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition]].<ref name=":0" />

==Awards and honors==
In 2005, Alexanderson won both one of the [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]],<ref name="maa"/><ref>[http://www.maa.org/node/119508 Haimo Award citation], [[Mathematical Association of America]], retrieved 2014-06-26.</ref> and the Yueh-Gin Gung and Dr. Charles Y. Hu Award for Distinguished Service to Mathematics,<ref name="maa"/><ref>{{citation|title=Yueh-Gin Gung and Dr. Charles Y. Hu Award to Gerald L. Alexanderson for Distinguished Service to Mathematics|first=Robert E.|last=Megginson|authorlink= Robert Megginson |journal=[[American Mathematical Monthly]]|volume=112|issue=3|date=March 2005|pages=197–199|doi=10.2307/30037437|jstor=30037437}}.</ref> both from the Mathematical Association of America.
